verdict.rationale: The UCP protocol that Shopify's agent surface is built on documents AP2 payment mandates and verifiable credentials. These let agents transact within pre-defined, verifiable boundaries using signed authorizations tied to a specific cart state, which implies amount and merchant scoping. However, Shopify's own checkout docs only describe collecting a payment credential and advertise handlers like Google Pay, with no explicit Shopify-side AP2 mandate support. missing for 10: Shopify-documented support for AP2 mandates in its checkout, explicit amount-limit, expiry and merchant-restriction controls, a user-facing flow for issuing a scoped credential to an agent, hands-on or independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can hand my agent a scoped, limited-use payment credential — amount limits, expiry, merchant restrictions — instead of a raw card number

citations.quote: Allows autonomous AI agents to transact on behalf of users with pre-defined, verifiable boundaries.
allows Platforms to provide cryptographically signed payment authorizations that are mathematically tied to the specific state of the cart
secure payment (AP2) via payment mandates and verifiable credentials
